articles.title: Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone just survived a cancellation scare
articles.summary: Apple's rumored 20th-anniversary iPhone with a dramatic glass-centric design is still reportedly on track for a 2027 launch, despite recent claims that supply chain issues had forced the company to cancel the project. The design is expected to feature curved glass wrapping around the front, back, and sides of the device, with a metal band for structural support after more ambitious all-glass concepts proved impractical. Before then, Apple is expected to launch the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, its first foldable iPhone, and several other models. Incoming CEO John Ternus may use the 2027 redesign as a major statement for a new era of Apple hardware.

articles.title: Spotify will label ‘AI Persona' profiles and exclude their music from recommendations
articles.summary: Spotify will begin labeling AI-generated artist identities with “AI Persona” badges and exclude their music from editorial, algorithmic, and personalized recommendations unless users explicitly follow them. Starting in September, Spotify will identify AI Personas through self-disclosure and its own reviews, while allowing artists to appeal incorrect labels. The policy focuses on whether an artist's public identity represents a real person rather than how their music was created, as Spotify is trying to support AI-powered creativity while limiting low-quality AI-generated content.

articles.title: The new iOS 27 beta further expands Siri voice customization options
articles.summary: iOS 27 beta 5 expands Siri's new voice customization features, adding Pace and Expressivity controls to all American voices and existing British voices, rather than limiting them to the two new US voices introduced earlier. Users can now adjust speaking speed and emotional emphasis across 12 supported voices using five levels for each setting. The feature relies on a new on-device voice model and requires recent hardware. Siri AI itself is expected to launch in beta later this year on devices starting with the iPhone 15 Pro.

articles.title: The Dopamine Architecture: How UX Designers Hold User Attention in 2026
articles.summary: Dopamine is released in anticipation of a reward rather than on receiving it, which is why variable reward schedules appear far beyond gambling. Micro-animations, sound design, and near-miss effects convert waiting into anticipation and drive re-engagement. The frontier in 2026 is real-time personalization that adapts interfaces to inferred emotional state, outpacing existing ethical frameworks.

articles.title: Agile Design 101: How Teams Build Better Products Faster
articles.summary: Agile design breaks UX work into short sprints and relies on user feedback to refine each iteration before moving on. This guide compares it with traditional linear design, identifies which stakeholders to involve, and walks through the seven stages of a cycle. It also covers obstacles like design-development pacing and how AI is reshaping the designer's role.

articles.title: The new 7UP rebrand is bound to be contentious
articles.summary: 7UP has introduced a new brand identity and reformulated drink that shifts the flavor focus from lemon-and-lime to a more lime-forward profile, now marketed as “lime lemon.” The redesign features a cleaner, retro-inspired visual identity and is part of a broader effort to differentiate the brand and appeal to younger consumers, particularly Gen Z and Gen Alpha, who reportedly prefer citrus-forward flavors. While the refreshed look has been widely praised, the unusual “lime lemon” naming may prove more controversial than the branding itself.

articles.title: Ctruh Studio: XR Commerce Suite for Every Brand (Website)
articles.summary: Turn flat product pages into immersive shopping experiences, from one upload, live in minutes. From a single product image, publish the full immersive suite: interactive 3D, virtual try-ons, AR previews, immersive stores, 3D configurators, and AI-generated creatives.

articles.title: Step into the World of Interactive Content (Website)
articles.summary: Plethora is a world of tiny interactive bits: games, art, music, puzzles, toys, and strange little experiences.

articles.title: AI Video Ad Generator for Winning Social Ads (Website)
articles.summary: Turn a product URL or inspiration video into winning short-form ads. AdAnt helps teams plan, recreate, and generate social video ad variants at scale.

articles.title: Building design system components with agent teams
articles.summary: AI agent teams can be used to build complex, production-ready design system components from design files, using a challenging real-world example to test the limits of current AI-assisted workflows. Generating high-quality components requires more than a single prompt, especially when accessibility, design system standards, and product-level quality are involved. This guide focuses on the architecture, workflows, and lessons learned from building an agent-based system that combines automation with human oversight to achieve reliable results.

articles.title: Are You Designing for the Old World?
articles.summary: AI has changed how software gets built, but not yet what gets built. Design is moving from "Responsive Web Design" toward "Malleable Design," where users shape their own layouts, dashboards, and editors from a base. Making that shift means rethinking components as design harnesses and working out where governance fits in.

articles.title: Can Design Really Support Mental Wellbeing? Seven Projects Exploring the Question
articles.summary: Design's field of action is shifting from the body toward the mind, through devices that detect emotions, stress, and moods and translate them into data. Seven projects, among them a digital garden of inner states, a bag that pulses with the heartbeat, and a breathing lamp, turn the invisible into an interface. Whether such technologies deepen self-understanding or digitize inner life remains an open question.

articles.title: This Font Looks Perfectly Normal to Humans but Wreaks Havoc on AI
articles.summary: ShieldFont uses ligature-style substitutions to swap whole words in a page's HTML source, so scrapers collect decoy text while human readers see the original.

articles.title: Former McLaren Designers Bring Supercar Thinking to Furniture
articles.summary: Two former McLaren Automotive designers who worked on the W1 hypercar and Speedtail have applied supercar thinking to furniture with the Ennua Element 01.
